claims_disputed.claim: Current systems are far from reliable multimodal localization: best agent 38.96 file Acc@5 and 22.45 function Acc@10; best retriever 33.86 function Acc@10.
claims_disputed.reason: Table 2's percentages are single runs of strict all-gold Acc@K, which is zero unless every PR-edited location is inside K. §6 says that gold is the merged diff, not a minimal cause. The function Acc@10 winner is the authors' own retriever (33.86 versus Qwen3-VL-Emb-8B at 32.65).

pattern_stance_changes.reason: §5.1 compares OpenHands (98.6% valid JSON, 37.42 File@5) with Mini-SWE-Agent (47.1%, 18.71) on the same Claude model, but the step cap, finish action, and tool surface change together. CodeAct is used, not isolated.

missed_issues: Table 3 lists AgentLess with GPT-5.2 at 29.59 with-image File@5, while Table 4's Original cell for the same method and model is 28.15. Those should be the same image-present condition, and the paper does not explain the 1.44 point gap.
§3.2: six annotators labeled 450 instances in about 20 hours, with no agreement statistic, and 202 of 652 rows (31%) come from an unnamed VLM gate. Appendix C says 23 languages; §3.4 says 24.

The review does not tag P08. Table 4's image-to-text step helps AgentLess with Claude (25.15 to 28.53 File@5) and hurts LocAgent with GPT-5.2 (19.13 to 16.12), so structured visual text is a split result, not a default adapter. BM25 at 21.01 File@5 (Table 2) is also an untagged weak lexical baseline on this set.
note: The review correctly refuses the abstract's story that images explain the drop from SWE-bench file scores near 90 to multimodal scores near 40. Table 3 shows OpenHands with GPT-5.2 moving 0.31 File@5 when images are added, and Claude scoring higher without them. That visual-evidence claim is already weak and should stay weak; the 'far from reliable' headline should drop to weak because the metric and the self-trained function winner do a lot of the work. Relevance 4 is a bit high for a screenshot-heavy benchmark against a Java ingestion backend: the Java slice is 44 instances and file Acc@5 there is 39.53, almost the overall 38.96. JD.com affiliation with no JD product on the board is low, not a vendor grading its own product; the function-level win is still self-evaluation. Reproducibility 3 undersells a claimed dataset, prompts in the appendix, and per-instance predictions.
